extract.summary: This is a label from a pharmacy that tells the patient how to take their medicine.

terms.plain: Take the medicine two times every day.
There are 60 tablets in the bottle.
You can get this medicine from the pharmacy 2 more times.
Throw the medicine away after this date because it may not work.
This medicine should not be used because it could be harmful.

topic.title: Reading Your Label
topic.blurb: Let's learn how to understand the information on your medicine bottle.

frequency.name: How Often
frequency.review: The label tells you how many times a day to take the medicine. This helps you stay on track with your care.

quantity.name: Amount
quantity.review: The quantity (Qty) is the total number of pills in the bottle. This helps you know when you might run low.

refills.name: Getting More
refills.review: Refills are the number of times you can get more of the medicine from the pharmacy. Your care team decides how many refills you get.

expiration.name: Safety Dates
expiration.review: The 'discard after' date tells you when to throw the medicine away. Medicine may not work well after this date.

safety.name: Safety Warnings
safety.review: If a medicine is 'contraindicated,' it means it should not be used. This is because it could be harmful to the patient.

questions.prompt: If a label says 'Twice daily,' what does that mean?
options: Take the medicine every two days.
Take the medicine two times every day.
Take the medicine only two times total.
Take the medicine twice a week.
questions.explain: Twice daily means the medicine is taken two times each day.

questions.prompt: You see 'Qty: 60' on a bottle. What is this telling you?
options: Take 60 pills at once.
There are 60 tablets in the bottle.
The medicine lasts for 60 days.
You can refill the bottle 60 times.
questions.explain: The Qty or quantity tells you how many tablets are inside the bottle.

questions.prompt: What does 'Refills: 2' mean on a prescription label?
options: You should refill the bottle every 2 days.
The bottle contains 2 pills.
You must take the medicine 2 times.
You can get this medicine from the pharmacy 2 more times.
questions.explain: Refills tell you how many more times the pharmacy can give you the medicine.

questions.prompt: Why should you follow the 'Discard after' date on a label?
options: To change how often the medicine is taken.
Because the medicine may not work after that date.
Because the pharmacy will stop refills.
To make room for new medicine.
questions.explain: It is important to throw medicine away after this date because it may no longer work.

questions.prompt: If a medicine is 'Contraindicated,' what does that mean?
options: The medicine should be taken with food.
The medicine is free of charge.
The medicine is very strong.
The medicine should not be used because it could be harmful.
questions.explain: Contraindicated is a word used to say a medicine should not be used because it could be harmful.
